The compact configuration (h1, h2) = (64, 16) is used for all equilibrium small-molecule benchmarks. The other columns of Table S3 re-quote earlier papers. Table X of Pfau et al. labels the coordinates 'Position (a_0)', but they are in angstrom (C-N 1.464, C-H 1.100; in bohr the C-N bond would be 0.77 angstrom), and the instance stores them in angstrom; the energies near CCSD(T)/CBS confirm the angstrom geometry.

results.system_description: N₂ at the geometry 'R = 1.6 bohr', all electrons, 7 up and 7 down electrons, clamped nuclei
results.variant: NucleoNet, (h1, h2) = (128, 32), trained jointly on the 32-point N₂ grid
results.source_location: Supplementary Material, Table S5 (tab:n2_full_energies), row L = 1.6000 a_0
results.eligibility_evidence: VMC energy of the paper's own NucleoNet, one model 'optimized jointly on 32 bond lengths ... and evaluated on the same grid' (multi-geometry, eligible under P5); not quoted, not extrapolated. The paper does not describe a separate evaluation run (local-energy clipping is listed only as a VMC training setting, Table S1).
results.notes: Multi-geometry (transferable) training mode; Table S5 prints only this jointly optimized column (no single-geometry N2 grid). Widths (h1, h2) = (128, 32) from Table S2 'Multi-geometry systems'; batch 128 x 32 (Table S4); HF pretraining used. Geometry printed in the paper, grid defined by the paper (no external dataset named); interior bond lengths are 4-decimal roundings of the uniform grid. Sector not stated; singlet N_up = N_down = 7 assumed. Parenthesized error: 'values in parentheses denote the statistical uncertainty in the last reported digit' (Table S5-S7 captions); the kind of statistical error is not specified, so 'unspecified' as for the existing NucleoNet rows. Grid endpoint: the printed value is exact.
